FAQs
General
What is EntityLocker and how is it different from DigiLocker for partner organizations?

EntityLocker is a secure digital document wallet developed for entities such as businesses, MSMEs, startups, trusts, societies, and government organizations. While DigiLocker facilitates the issuance, storage, and sharing of authenticated documents for individual citizens, EntityLocker enables organizations to securely access, manage, and share entity-related documents and certificates issued by government departments and other authorized issuers. The platform supports role-based access, multiple authorized users, and consent-based document sharing, thereby reducing reliance on physical documentation and enabling secure, paperless verification and exchange of organizational records.

Organizations and entities can register on EntityLocker via the Sign up page to securely access and manage their digital documents.

Government departments, regulators, financial institutions, and other organizations can integrate with EntityLocker through the APISetu platform as Issuers or Requesters to issue, access, and verify authenticated entity documents digitally. Become a partner.

How do we register as a partner organization for DigiLocker or EntityLocker through APISetu, and what documents are required?

To register as a partner organization on APISetu, visit the partner portal and sign up using your DigiLocker account. After registration, organizations can apply to onboard as an Issuer (to publish documents or APIs) or a Requester (to access and verify documents or data, subject to applicable permissions).

Depending on the onboarding category, submit a valid use case and the required onboarding documents, including Proof of Identity, Authority Letter, Organization PAN, GST Registration Certificate, Certificate of Incorporation, etc. Following review and approval, the onboarding team will facilitate API subscription, provide the necessary credentials, and support the organization through the integration process.

For detailed onboarding guidelines and document requirements, please refer to DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

Video to be showcased: Partner Onboarding Process for DigiLocker | Step-by-Step Guide | DigiLocker | Digital India

My account is not approved yet. How long does organization account approval take, and what is the status check process?

Organization account approval timelines may vary depending on the completeness of the application, verification of submitted documents, and review requirements. Applicants are advised to ensure that all required information and supporting documents have been submitted accurately.

For updates on the status of an application, organizations may contact the partner support team at partners[at]digitallocker[dot]gov[dot]in using their registered email address.

For technical assistance and onboarding support, organizations may join the daily technical VC conducted from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM (Monday to Saturday). The video consultation facility is available exclusively for entities, partners, and organizations.

How can we contact the DigiLocker / EntityLocker partner support team?

Organizations requiring assistance with DigiLocker or EntityLocker partner onboarding, integration, or operational queries may contact the partner support team via:

Email Support: Write to partners[at]digitallocker[dot]gov[dot]in using the registered email address, along with the Organization Name, Client ID/Application Reference Number (if applicable), a brief description of the issue, and any relevant screenshots or supporting documents.
Technical VC: Join the daily technical VC conducted from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM (Monday to Saturday). The video consultation facility is available exclusively for entities, partners, and organizations.
Where can we find the latest API documentation, specifications, and integration guides?

The latest API documentation, technical specifications, onboarding resources, and integration guides are available on DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

Partner organizations are advised to refer to these repositories regularly to access the latest implementation guidelines, API specifications, sample code, onboarding documents, and other integration-related resources.

What is the maximum number of Client IDs that can be added to the Partner Portal?

Organizations may create up to 10 Client IDs within the Partner Portal.

How do I find the Client ID and client configuration?

Partner organizations can view or provision their Client ID and client configuration parameters by following these steps within the portal:

To View Configuration:

Log into the Partner portal.
Navigate to the Consume APIs section on the left menu of the dashboard.
Click on MeriPehchaan Auth to view the active Client ID and configuration attributes.

To Generate New Credentials:

Click on the Add Authpartner button located on the top right of the dashboard.
Enter the required integration details.
Click the Add button to complete the generation process.
How do we get API credentials?

DigiLocker and EntityLocker API credentials, including the Organisation ID (orgId) and API Key, are provisioned through the APISetu Partner portal as part of the onboarding process and become available after successful approval and application configuration. Organizations may access these credentials through the partner dashboard and use them in accordance with the applicable integration guidelines and approval process.

For detailed onboarding guidelines and document requirements, please refer to DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

What authentication method is used and how do we generate access tokens?

DigiLocker and EntityLocker APIs use the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework along with OpenID Connect (OIDC) for authentication and identity verification. Access tokens are generated through the prescribed OAuth 2.0 authorization flow after successful user authentication and consent, where applicable.

Partner organizations are required to implement the authentication flow in accordance with the technical specifications and integration guidelines provided as part of the onboarding process. For detailed onboarding guidelines, please refer to DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

What data format will I receive when fetching the access token?

When fetching the access token, you will receive the data in a JSON string format. Depending on the specific endpoint configuration your application implements, the exact fields structured within that JSON payload will vary.

For detailed onboarding guidelines, please refer to DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

Is IP whitelisting required?

No, IP whitelisting is not required for API integration. You can securely access and interact with the endpoints without needing to submit your server's static IP address for whitelisting.

How long does integration usually take?

The time required for integration may vary depending on factors such as the complexity of the use case, readiness of the integrating system, availability of required resources, and timely completion of onboarding and testing activities.

Partner organizations are encouraged to review the available documentation at DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center, participate in technical consultation sessions, and coordinate with the concerned teams to facilitate a smooth and timely integration process.

What is the difference between issued documents and self-uploaded documents?

Issued Documents are digital documents issued directly by authorized issuers, such as government departments, regulatory bodies, or other approved organizations, and are available in a digitally verifiable format through DigiLocker or EntityLocker. These documents are considered authentic electronic records and carry the same legal validity as their physical counterparts in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Self-Uploaded Documents are documents uploaded by users or organizations for storage, access, and sharing purposes. These documents are not issued or verified by an authorized issuer through the platform and do not constitute authenticated electronic records issued through DigiLocker or EntityLocker.

How to map Pull URI in DigiLocker or EntityLocker integration?

The Pull URI is configured during issuer onboarding and is mapped to the issuer's document repository and document types. Organizations are required to implement the Pull URI Request API in accordance with the Issuer API Specification and ensure that the endpoint returns the appropriate Document URI(s) based on the search parameters received from DigiLocker or EntityLocker.

For detailed onboarding guidelines and configuration requirements, please refer to the API Specification documents available in the DigiLocker Resource Center and EntityLocker Resource Center.

What should we check when we get a 401 or 403 error?

HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) errors indicate that the authentication credentials provided with the request are invalid, missing, or expired, while HTTP 403 (Forbidden) errors indicate that the request has been authenticated but the application does not have the necessary permissions or access rights to perform the requested operation.

Organizations are advised to verify their API credentials, access token, subscribed APIs, configured scopes, and application settings before retrying the request. If the issue persists, organizations may contact the partner support team:

Email Support: Write to partners[at]digitallocker[dot]gov[dot]in using the registered email address, along with the Organization Name, Client ID/Application Reference Number (if applicable), a brief description of the issue, error message, timestamps, and any relevant screenshots or supporting documents.
Technical VC: Join the daily technical VC conducted from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM (Monday to Saturday). The video consultation facility is available exclusively for entities, partners, and organizations.
What are the common integration errors (e.g., scope not found, account not found) and how can they be resolved?

Common integration issues may arise due to configuration mismatches, incorrect API parameters, invalid credentials, incomplete onboarding, or access and permission-related settings. Organizations are advised to review the applicable API documentation, verify their integration configuration, and ensure that the required permissions and credentials have been correctly configured.

If the issue persists, organizations may contact the partner support team:

Email Support: Write to partners[at]digitallocker[dot]gov[dot]in using the registered email address, along with the Organization Name, Client ID/Application Reference Number (if applicable), a brief description of the issue, error message, timestamps, and any relevant screenshots or supporting documents.
Technical VC: Join the daily technical VC conducted from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM (Monday to Saturday). The video consultation facility is available exclusively for entities, partners, and organizations.
What logs should we submit when reporting an issue to the support team?

When reporting an issue to the support team, organizations are advised to provide sufficient information to facilitate timely investigation and resolution. This may include the Organization Name, Client ID/Application Reference Number (if applicable), API name, request timestamp, error message or response code, request/transaction ID (if available), and relevant screenshots or log extracts.

Organizations should ensure that sensitive information, such as API keys, access tokens, passwords, or personally identifiable information (PII), is not shared in support requests.

Support requests may be submitted to partners[at]digitallocker[dot]gov[dot]in using the registered organizational email address.

How are API updates and scheduled maintenance communicated to partners?

API updates, service advisories, and scheduled maintenance notifications are communicated to partner organizations through their registered email addresses.

Banking
What is the end-to-end flow for accessing an e-BG through Entity Locker, and what are the roles of the Bank, Applicant, Beneficiary, NeSL, and Entity Locker?

The end-to-end flow is:

Bank issues the e-BG on the NeSL platform and captures consent from the applicant and beneficiary;
consent state is recorded with NeSL;
the entity logs in to its Entity Locker;
entity triggers a fetch request in Entity Locker;
NeSL validates consent for that entity and e-BG;
on a positive match, the e-BG is rendered in the entity's Entity Locker.

Roles: the Bank is the Data Fiduciary and issuer; the Applicant and Beneficiary are the consenting entities/Data Principals who access their own lockers; NeSL operates the e-BG source platform and serves the consent-validated pull; and Entity Locker (NeGD) provides the secure, consent-gated storage and retrieval interface. A detailed swim-lane diagram can be appended as Annexure I.

How will consent management work for e-BGs, and will consent be one-time or transaction-specific?

Consent will be obtained by the issuing Bank from the applicant at the time of e-BG issuance, in line with Section 5 read with Section 6 of the DPDP Act, 2023. This consent authorises NeSL to make the e-BG available, through Entity Locker, to the applicant and the named beneficiary, where they have Entity Locker accounts. Where the applicant or beneficiary is a registered entity (corporate/MSME), the natural person authorized to act for that entity exercises consent on its behalf.

A digital log is created when consent is given, specifying the exact e-BG and the reason for access. NeSL uses this log to verify and authorize all document retrieval requests. The Entity Locker will only show the e-BG to accounts that hold active consent. Essentially, without explicit consent, the document remains completely invisible.

Consent is transaction-specific by design. Each e-BG carries its own consent linkage, consistent with the DPDP principle of purpose limitation. A blanket, one-time consent is not used as the default, because it would not satisfy the requirement that consent be specific to a defined purpose. Where a customer relationship warrants it, the Bank may operationally capture consent at onboarding, but the consent must still map to each e-BG made available.

How is consent status validated and enforced before e-BG documents are made available through Entity Locker?

The Entity Locker Document Pull request to NeSL is gated on a consent check and follows a default-denied access model. Before any e-BG document is rendered, the system confirms that a valid, un-withdrawn consent exists for that specific e-BG and that specific entity, conveyed through the same consent-status interface.

The document is only released if the details match. If the consent is absent, expired, or withdrawn, the pull is not served.

Is separate consent required from both the applicant and the beneficiary, and how can the Bank collect beneficiary consent?

An electronic Bank Guarantee (e-BG) is inherently a tripartite framework involving the bank, the applicant, and the beneficiary; the Bank will be required to integrate consent collection into this existing lifecycle. The explicit consent the Bank is required to obtain is from the applicant, at the time of issuance, authorising access to the e-BG via Entity Locker for both the applicant and the beneficiary, where they are registered.

Beneficiary-side access to its own Entity Locker is handled through the Entity Locker / NeSL onboarding and authentication flows, not necessarily through a separate consent collected by the issuing Bank. Where the Bank independently determines that it is a Data Fiduciary for beneficiary personal data in the issuance process, it must comply with the DPDP Act for that processing as well; however, it does not mandate that the Bank obtain a separate locker-specific consent directly from non-customer beneficiaries.

The Bank shall embed beneficiary consent into the e-BG application form facilitated by the applicant. Specifically, when the beneficiary accepts the e-BG terms, either through the NeSL platform or via the underlying contract requirements, their explicit consent to retrieve documents via Entity Locker can be embedded directly into the initial e-BG application and agreement forms facilitated by the applicant. By utilizing this applicant-led routing and leveraging a lightweight digital authentication gateway via NeSL, the Bank will efficiently maintain its position as the single point of responsibility for consent management and grievance redressal.

What happens when consent is withdrawn or modified, and what is the impact on already-issued or previously accessed e-BGs?

Consent withdrawal/modification is to be initiated through the Bank (as Data Fiduciary) and reflected to NeSL, which updates the consent state. The Bank should reflect a withdrawal to NeSL promptly so that prospective access is blocked at the next access attempt; the integration supports near-real-time state updates. The Entity Locker honours the updated state at the next access attempt. Withdrawal is to be as easy to exercise as the grant of consent, consistent with the DPDP Act.

Withdrawal operates prospectively. Upon withdrawal, the Entity Locker stops serving fresh access to the affected e-BG for the relevant entity from that point forward. The platform revokes prospective access. Operationally, withdrawal stops prospective Entity Locker access to the affected e-BG for the relevant entity; the legal validity and enforceability of the underlying bank guarantee is a separate matter and is not extinguished merely by a data-access withdrawal.

Copies that an entity may have already legitimately downloaded prior to withdrawal are outside the platform's control; what the system guarantees is that no further access is served once consent is withdrawn. What withdrawal stops is further disclosure, not the existence of audit records. Statutory record-retention obligations on the Bank are unaffected. Historical lifecycle/audit logs are retained as part of the integrity and auditability of the system and to meet record-keeping obligations.

Under the DPDP Act, 2023, 'Data Principal' rights, including the withdrawal of consent, are exercised by the natural persons authorized to act on behalf of the applicant or beneficiary entity. However, in the specific context of an e-BG, this right must be harmonized with underlying banking laws and the irrevocable nature of financial guarantees. While a Data Principal may prospectively withdraw consent to stop further automated visibility or background replication of the document within the Entity Locker platform, such data-centric withdrawal operates strictly on a prospective basis. It does not extinguish, suspend, or override the independent statutory, regulatory, or contractual obligations governing the active bank guarantee itself.

To prevent financial risk or systemic misuse, the Bank will process consent withdrawals in a manner that ensures the integrity, enforceability, and lifecycle tracking of the underlying e-BG contract remain entirely unaffected. As the Data Fiduciary, the Bank is responsible for receiving and actioning withdrawal requests and ensuring the updated consent state is promptly reflected to NeSL. System-driven controls (such as a default-deny state on consent change) apply automatically to gate Document Pull requests, and robust status/audit logging is maintained, with configurable alerts provided as part of the system integration.

Will existing e-BGs be available through Entity Locker, and can an e-BG still be issued if consent is not provided?

For previously issued e-BGs, availability through Entity Locker is contingent on obtaining the requisite consent for those e-BGs. Newly issued e-BGs follow the consent-at-issuance flow. The differentiator is the presence of valid consent, not the issuance date.

Issuance and lifecycle management of an e-BG on the NeSL platform is distinct from making the e-BG viewable through Entity Locker. The e-BG can be issued and processed on the usual legal bases available to the Bank (such as performance of contract or compliance with law), even if the applicant does not consent to Entity Locker-based access. If this consent is not given, the e-BG remains fully operational in the existing NeSL repository and portal; only the Entity Locker visibility for that e-BG is withheld.

What are the Bank's DPDP responsibilities, and why is the Bank the single point of contact for data principal rights and grievances?

Under the DPDP Act, 2023, the entity that determines the purpose and means of data processing is the Data Fiduciary. Because the issuing Bank decides how customer data is collected, how the e-BG is generated, and when to authorize its digital dissemination, it naturally meets this statutory test. Consequently, primary responsibilities for lawful collection, verifiable consent, data minimization, and accuracy rest with the Bank.

Data Principal rights are legally owed by the Data Fiduciary. Because the core customer relationship and the underlying consent management sit exclusively with the issuing Bank, the Bank is statutorily required to be the single point of contact for grievance redressal. Conversely, since MeitY's Entity Locker operates strictly as a neutral digital repository and "wallet" infrastructure, any platform-specific technical faults, such as login, interface rendering, or portal availability errors, remain within the control of and will be directly handled by NeSL or NeGD.

In contrast, NeSL and Entity Locker act as Data Processors or infrastructure providers that store and transmit data solely to execute the Bank's instructions and the user's consent. Accordingly, the sought declaration and indemnity focus strictly on areas within the Bank's operational control, namely, the legality of the e-BG data and the validity of the underlying consent management. They are not intended to make the Bank liable for operational or security failures originating within the NeSL or Entity Locker platforms themselves, for which the Bank is not liable.

While access remains restricted to the applicant and beneficiary, moving the full e-BG lifecycle to Entity Locker changes the data processing architecture from on-demand viewing to automated, platform-wide routing. As the Data Fiduciary under the DPDP Act, 2023, the Bank requires explicit, purpose-specific authorization to legally enable this automated background replication. Securing this upfront consent unlocks the Government's Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living objectives, allowing Corporate and MSME beneficiaries to experience seamless, real-time tracking of renewals and amendments in a single digital wallet without manual intervention.

Is the one-time institutional declaration mandatory, and will it impact existing NeSL e-BG operations or require system changes?

No. The declaration is required only for banks that wish to enable Entity Locker access for their customers. It governs the consent-gated sharing layer. A bank that does not wish to offer Entity Locker access is not required to submit it.

Core e-BG issuance and lifecycle management on the NeSL portal continue unaffected. The declaration is additive and pertains solely to the optional Entity Locker integration. Portal-specific technical faults (login, rendering, availability of the Entity Locker interface) are handled by NeSL/NeGD as the platform operators. The Bank remains the point of contact for consent- and data-related queries concerning the e-BG it issued. Responsibilities are split along the same control line as liability.

The core NeSL onboarding remains as-is. The incremental change is the consent-capture step associated with enabling Entity Locker availability; this is layered onto, rather than replacing, existing onboarding. The required system changes are minimal. The integration is pull-based and designed to limit changes at the bank end. The principal new requirement is supporting consent capture and relaying consent state (where the consent-status API is adopted). Any specific touchpoints will be detailed in the integration specification.

The declaration should be executed by an officer duly authorised to bind the Bank, typically an authorised signatory empowered by Board resolution or power of attorney, of a sufficiently senior grade.

How do Entity Locker accounts work, who manages them, and what reference materials are available for onboarding banks?

Entity Locker is an enterprise-facing digital wallet operated by MeitY/NeGD, which owns the storage layer, manages user credentials, and provides the secure interface where users give consent. Conversely, NeSL acts as the financial data repository and execution engine that generates and securely holds the e-BG.

The system operates via a pull-based handshake architecture: the e-BG remains stored in NeSL's secure database, and when a registered corporate user logs into their Entity Locker to "fetch" a document, MeitY transmits the user's explicit digital consent token to NeSL. NeSL instantly validates this token against its stored consent logs and delivers the specific e-BG to be rendered directly within the user's Entity Locker interface.

The entity accesses its Entity Locker through its own authenticated Entity Locker credentials (established during the entity's Entity Locker onboarding), not through credentials issued by the Bank.

NeSL has issued Circular No. NeSL/DDE/2026/235 dated 05.05.2026, regarding the availability of Electronic Bank Guarantees (e-BGs) through Entity Locker. Additionally, MeitY and NeSL have publicly announced the integration through press releases dated 19.01.2025 and 07.10.2025.

The integration specification, process flow diagrams (Annexure I), institutional declaration format (Annexure I of the MeitY letter), and standardized consent artefact (Annexure III) will be shared with onboarding banks as part of the formal documentation package. A consolidated reference set including all circulars, public advisories, and technical specifications can be provided on request.

DigiLocker aims at ‘Digital Empowerment’ of the citizen by providing access to authentic digital documents to the citizen’s digital document wallet.
